rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Gameplay 3 Special Tiles 4 End of Game 5 Variants 5.1 Other Board Setups Objective That's life (or Verflixxt) is a game of tile collecting. There are plus and minus tiles which will score or deduct points. Getting too many minuses? Use the actions and lucky tiles! At the end the player with the highest score wins. Gameplay All tiles are shuffled and the board is built. There is an action tile after each 8 tiles. Everyone has 3 pieces at the start. Guards will not be used in the basic version. On your turn, roll a dice (1-6) and move any of your pieces that number of steps. If you move a piece off a tile where it was the only one, you must take that tile (even if it is negative). The start tile can't be collected. Remove it from the track and place it in front of you, face-up. This is the start of your tile tower. When you collect other tiles, put them on top of your tile tower. You cannot change the order of the tiles. After a tile is taken, close the gap in the track by pushing the other tiles together. Special Tiles Gift action: Take the top tile of your tower. If it is minus, give it to the player who has the most valuable top. Else give it to the player who has the least valuable top. The tile is then flipped over to the steal side. If you have no tiles just flip over the tile. Steal action: Take the top tile from any player’s tower of your choice and put it on top of your own tower. Flip the tile from the Steal side to the Gift side. If none of the other players has any tiles just flip over the tile. Lucky tile: For each lucky tile in your tower, you may change one minus tile to a plus tile. Extra lucky tiles have no effect. End of Game If a piece is moved to the finish tile it cannot be moved any more. If a player has all their tiles moved onto the finish tile the player doesn't take any more turns. When all the pieces are moved to the finish tile the game is over. The player with the highest score wins. If there is a tie, the player with least number of lucky tiles wins. If there is still a, tie they remain tied. Variants Action tile: You can choose not to add any action tiles. Expert scoring: The lucky tiles convert the tile below them in the stack into the opposite. Guards: There are guards on the lucky, +7 and +8 tiles. You may choose to move a guard instead of your piece, if it is sharing a tile with a player's piece. You cannot collect tiles with guards on it. Other Board Setups Standard sorted: -1 to -8, lucky tiles, +8 to +1, -1 to -10. Variant 1: -1 to -8, +1 to +8, lucky tiles, -1 to -10. Variant 2: -1 to -8, +1 to +8, -1 to -10, lucky tiles.

[Rating: 1/10] It's roll and move with random screwage of the other players.  A pretty depressing and cynical take on life.

[Rating: 2/10] ALL LUCK...I easly won my first game (on BSW) WHILE I was reading the rules at the same time...yea, that says a lot...

[Rating: 2/10] Not my kind of game.  Die rolls rule everything.  The best moves for any given roll are blatantly obvious.  Occassionally there may be a small decision to make, but generally, it's always clear what the right move is.  You could get the same results sitting by yourself, rolling dice, and moving the pieces of your imaginary opponents - the game is that automatic.

[Rating: 2/10] I have only played this once and I am sure that I had an unfortunate experience but this was not fun - I couldn't roll the right numbers at all. Not one I am looking forward to playing again. Update: I have now played this twice and had a second horrible gaming experience - there shall not be a third

[Rating: 2/10] Dice rolling and simple blocking game. Steal, gift, collect positive and negative points. Need to play with blockers. Simple blocking game.

[Rating: 3/10] Too abstract to be fun for kids (I tried it with them), and not engaging enough for adults (at least, not for me or my friends.)  Zero fun factor for us. We love Cartagena, but couldn't get into this one at all.

[Rating: 3/10] Played only on BSW. Quite a nice attempt at making a quality roll-and-move game that largely succeeds, but it just can't hold up to much repeat play, and the length of a game is a bit too much for something that is fundamentally pretty light.  UPDATE: Okay, I'm played out.  Rating dropped to 4.  UPDATE: make that a 3.

[Rating: 3/10] Too much luck, too little to do.  You have a few choices for the 1st half of the game, but you have little or no conrol (luck predominates) as the game progresses.  2 plays with standard setup.

[Rating: 3/10] Suppose to be fun, but it isn't.  Just roll a die to find who is the winner and let's play something else.

[Rating: 3/10] WOW!!  What a pure luck game...  Total randomness + lack of interesting decisions = I defnitely avoid it.  --  I might give it a shot with the expansion.  I vaguely recall a relaxing, nice game, some interesting choices and not excessive amount of luck when playing with it.

[Rating: 3/10] Described in a nutshell.  Roll your die and move.  There is some limited strategy in this game, but not a ton.  Extremely simple game rules (too simple for my tastes), easy enough for anyone to learn.  Good components.  Other than that, not much else.
